name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.exists_isolated_character_ne_infinity
title: An isolated character away from the scalar character

content.display_title: An isolated character away from the scalar character
content.one_sentence_role: Finds an isolated point in the open complement of the distinguished scalar character.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed. On $\widetilde A=\mathbb C\oplus A$, write $\chi_\infty(\lambda,a)=\lambda$. Let $D$ be a norm-closed commutative unital $*$-subalgebra of $\widetilde A$, and assume its character space $X$ is countable. Let $d\in D$ be nonzero and have scalar coordinate zero. Then there is $\chi\in X$ distinct from the scalar character $\chi_\infty|_D$ such that $\{\chi\}$ is open in $X$.
content.assumptions: This theorem has no representation $\pi$ or singleton-representation hypothesis. Countability of the character space is an explicit input.
content.conclusion: The same character is both different from the distinguished scalar character and isolated in the full character space.
content.proof_summary: Use the nonzero element to show that the complement of the scalar character is nonempty, apply the countable Baire lemma in that open subspace, and transfer openness back.
proof_steps: If every character vanished on $d$, its Gelfand transform would be zero. Injectivity of the Gelfand transform would then give $d=0$, a contradiction. Thus some $\chi_0$ satisfies $\chi_0(d)\ne0$. The scalar character has value zero at $d$ by the given scalar-coordinate condition, so $\chi_0\ne\chi_\infty|_D$.

Set $U=X\setminus\{\chi_\infty|_D\}$. The character space of the unital commutative $C^*$-algebra $D$ is compact Hausdorff; hence the distinguished singleton is closed and $U$ is open. Step 1 shows $U\ne\varnothing$. It is countable and $T_1$ as a subspace of $X$, and it is Baire, since an open subspace of this locally compact Hausdorff space is locally compact Hausdorff.

Apply [An isolated point in a nonempty countable Baire space](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Topology/CountableBaire.lean#L18-L28) to this very subspace $U$, using the four properties just verified. It supplies $\chi\in U$ for which $\{\chi\}$ is open in $U$. The inclusion of an open subspace is an open map, so the same singleton is open in $X$. Membership in $U$ is precisely $\chi\ne\chi_\infty|_D$.
